independent_review.why_this_scope_is_high_risk: This is the most latitude-dense material in Clause 11. DO CONCURRENT grants the processor substantial freedom over iteration order, and the locality rules are intricate enough that a plausible paraphrase is almost certainly wrong. The failure modes are an order-detecting plan, a floating-point reduction oracle, and reading a variable whose locality leaves it undefined.

locality_rules.status: independently derived by the reviewer from the source BEFORE comparing with the catalogue
locality_rules.classes: LOCAL, LOCAL_INIT, REDUCE, SHARED, or unspecified.
locality_rules.local: A variable with LOCAL locality is a construct entity; the outside variable is inaccessible by that name within the construct. At the start of each iteration, if it is a pointer it has undefined pointer association status, and otherwise it is undefined except for any subobjects that are default-initialized.
locality_rules.local_init: Takes the pointer association status and definition status of the outside variable of that name.
locality_rules.reduce: A construct entity whose initial value comes from Table 11.1; the final update combines the values from completed iterations, and the processor MAY COMBINE THEM IN ANY ORDER.
locality_rules.shared: Appearances refer to the variable in the innermost executable construct or scoping unit.
locality_rules.unspecified: References, definitions, pointer and allocatable uses must satisfy the listed same-iteration or no-other-iteration obligations; multiple definitions or pointer changes leave the status undefined after termination.
locality_rules.table_11_1: Verified row by row against the table itself, since extraction interleaves its columns.
locality_rules.undefined_state_discipline: No plan reads, compares or inquires about a LOCAL variable in its undefined state - that would not be a conforming program. The unobservability claim is scoped precisely to that state and does not suppress what is observable, such as the final value of a SHARED or REDUCE variable after the construct.

permissions.detail: Concurrent limit and step expressions may be evaluated in any order.
DO CONCURRENT iterations may occur in any order. No order oracle is permitted.
The processor may combine REDUCE values in any order.
Sequential record ordering across iterations is processor dependent.

permissions_verdict: All five verified in both directions. No plan infers an iteration order, counts invocations, relies on a side effect, or observes a temporary.

reduce_floating_point_exclusion.issue: Because the processor may combine reduction values in ANY ORDER, and real and complex values are approximations under 7.4.3 with mathematically equivalent rewriting permitted by 10.1.5.2.4, a REDUCE result over reals is order-sensitive and cannot be a value oracle.
reduce_floating_point_exclusion.verdict: correctly excluded. Only order-insensitive integer and logical reductions are planned.

ownership_boundaries.parallel_11_1_7_1_to_3: Those sections own the DO construct's purpose and form, loop-control syntax, construct names, the active and inactive concept, and the iteration-count rule. This packet owns execution after the DO statement: initiation, DO CONCURRENT active combinations, the execution cycle, CYCLE execution, termination, locality, reduction, shared and unspecified semantics, and the 11.1.7.5 restrictions. No catalogue was added for 11.1.7, 11.1.7.4 or 11.1.7.1 through .3.
ownership_boundaries.registered_forall: 10.2.4.x retains ownership of FORALL active-combination execution, assignment staging, statement sequencing and its own order permissions. This packet applies analogous safeguards to DO CONCURRENT without duplicating FORALL assignment semantics.
